column2: Phu is in blowing and in the fruitless; "vi" is a bird; "bha" is a star; "ma" is Shri, measure and mother; "ya" is in going and in the opposer of foes;
ra is in fire; "la" in Indra; "la" is called in the Creator; "va" in separation and Varuna, in lying; "sha" and "sham" in happiness;
sha in the best; "sa" in the unseen, and "sa" with Lakshmi; "sam" is held in hair; "ha" in bearing and in Rudra; "ksha" is held in Kshatriya and in the imperishable;
ksha is in Narasimha and in Hari, and likewise in the field-guardians. The one-syllable mantra deity gives enjoyment and liberation:
Homage to Haihaya-shirasa is the mantra giving all knowledge. Likewise mantras beginning with "a" — the Matrika mantra is the best.
On a single lotus one should worship these and the nine Durgas: Bhagavati, Katyayani, Kaushiki and Chandika,
Prachanda, Suranayika, Ugra, Parvati and Durga. "Om, we know Chandika, we meditate on Bhagavati; may that Durga impel us" — in order the six-limbed; the gana, the teacher, the teacher in order.
Ajita, Aparajita, Jaya, Vijaya; Katyayani, Bhadrakali, Mangala, Siddha, Revati;
Siddha and the other Vatukas are to be worshipped, Hetuka and Kapalika, Ekapada, Bhimarupa; the nine world-guardians in the middle.
Hrim, Durge Durge, protector, svaha for success of the mantra-meaning. Gauri is to be worshipped, and the powers beginning with Dharma and Skanda;
Prajna, Jnana, Kriya, Vacha, Vagishi, Jvalini, Kamini, Kamamala and the like; worship of the powers of Indra and the rest.
Om gam svaha is this root mantra, or "gam, homage to Ganapati." Six-limbed, red and white, with tusk, rosary, axe and ...;
with modaka, then in order "to Gandha, to Gandholka"; Gaja, Mahaganapati, Maholka are to be worshipped.

To Kushmanda, Ekadanta, Tripurantaka, Shyamadanta, Vikata, Harahasa, Lambanashanana, Padmadamshtra, Megholka, Dhumolka, Vakratunda, Vighneshvara, Vikatotkata, Gajendragamana, Bhujagendrahara, Shashankadhara, lord of the hosts, svaha. Having worshipped with these mantras ending in "svaha," with sesame oblation and the rest one shares wealth; or with those beginning with "ka" joined with seeds, and those beginning with them ending in "namah."
The mantras may be separate or each (garbled phrase on double-faced). What Katyayana and Skanda said — that grammar I shall tell.
U — "uttishtha"; "kavi etau"; "vayu etau"; "vane ime"; "ami ete"; "yajnabhute"; "ehi deva"; "iman naya" (examples of vowel sandhi and non-combination).
I shall tell the sandhi of consonants, speech controlled, with one mora: these six; "tad ime" and "vadi" — Vagniti, Shanmukha and the rest.
Vanmanasam, "vagbhava" and the rest; "vak shlakshnam", "tacchariraka"; "tallunati", "taccharet", "krunnaste", "sugannih" (examples of consonant sandhi).
Bhavamscharan, "bhavamschhatrah," "bhavamstikah," "bhavamsthakah," "bhavamstirtham," "bhavamstheyat," "bhavamllekha," "bhavanjayah" (examples).
Bhavanchhete, "bhavanchashete," "bhavanshete," "bhavandinah," "svambharta," "tvankaroshi" and the like — sandhi arising from visarga is to be known.
Kashchhindyat, "kashcharet," "kashtah," "kashthah," "kasthash cha," "kashchalet," "kah khanet," "kah karoti sma," "kah pathet" (visarga sandhi examples).
Kashshvashurah, "kahshvashurah," "kassavarah," "kahsavarah," "kah phalet," "kah shayita," "ko 'tra yodhah," "ka uttamah" (examples).
Deva ete bho iha, "sodara yanti bhago vraja," "supuh sudurat," "ratrir atra," "vayur yati punar na hi" (examples).
Punareti sa yatiha eshah yati ka ishvarah, "jyotirupam tavachchhatram," "mlechchhadhis chhidram achchhidat" (examples).
The first case is for address and for the agent or action in the unexpressed; what is done as the object — the second case is remembered for the object.
That by which it is done is the instrument; the one who does is the agent. In the unexpressed by verb, kridanta and taddhita endings, the third case is for the instrument.
And for the agent; the fourth case is for the recipient: to whom one wishes to give is called the dative.
The ablative: that from which one departs or takes fear. The fifth case is for ablative; the sixth for own-owner relation and the rest.
What is the support is the locus; the seventh case there. In one meaning singular; in two meanings dual;
in many, plural. Now I tell the accomplished forms: vriksha, surya, ambuvaha, arka, hari, dvijatayah (declension examples).
Viprau, gajat, mahendrena, yamabhyam, analaih, ramaya, munivaryabhyam, kebhyah, dharmat, harau ratih (examples of cases).
Sharabhyam, pustakebhyash cha, arthasyeshvarayor gatih; balanam sajjane pritih, hamsayoh kamaleshu cha (examples).
Thus words such as kama and mahesha are to be known like vriksha. "Sarve, vishve cha, sarvasmai, sarvasmat, katarah" (pronoun forms) are held;
sarveshaam, svam, vishvasmin — the rest of the forms like vriksha. Thus also ubhaya, katara, katama, anyatara and the like.
Purve, purvash cha, purvasmai, purvasmat, susamagatah, purve, buddhish cha, purvasmin — the remaining forms like sarva (declension examples).
Thus apara, avara and the like, dakshina, uttara, antara; apara, adhara, nema; "prathamah, prathame" like arka.
Thus charama, ayata, alpa, ardha, nema and the like; "dvitiyasmai, dvitiyaya, dvitiyasmat, dvitiyakat" (declension examples);
dvitiyasmin, dvitiye cha, tritiyash cha like arka. "Somapah, somapau" are to be known: "somapah, somapam vraja" (declension of somapa);
kilalapau, somapash cha, somapa, somape dada, somapabhyam, somapebhyah, somapah, somapoh kulam (declension of somapa).
Thus kilalapa and the like; kavi, agni, ari: "he kave, kavim, agni tan harin satyakina hritam" (declension of kavi, agni).
Ravibhyam ravibhir dehi vahnaye yah samagatah; agneh, agnyoh, agninam, kavau, kavyoh, kavishu (declension of ravi, agni, kavi).
Thus susriti, abhranti, sukirti, sudhriti; sakha: "sakha, sakhayau, sakhayah, he sakhe, vraja satpatim" (declension of sakhi).
Sakhayam cha sakhayau cha sakhin sakhya gato dada; sakhye sakhyuh cha sakhyuh cha sakhyoh — the rest like kavi.
Patya, patye, patyuh, patyuh, patyoh like agni; "dvau dvau, dvabhyam dvabhyam, dvityadyarthe dvayor dvayoh" (declension of dvi).
Trayah, trin, tribhih, tribhyah, trayanam cha, trishu in order; like kavi: "kati, kati" — the rest is remembered as plural (declension of tri, kati).
Nih, niyau, niyah, he nih, niyam, niyah, niyah, niya; nibhyam, nibhih, niye, nibhyah, niyat, niyi, niyoh (declension of ni).
Susri, sudhi and the like, gramani: "one should worship Hari; gramanyau, gramanyah, gramanyam, gramanya, gramanibhih" (declension of gramani).
Gramanyah, gramanyam thus; senani and the like; subhu: "subhuvau, svayambhuvah, svayambhuvam, svayambhuvah" (declension).
Svayambhuva, svayambhuvi thus pratibhu and the like; khalapu: "khalapuh, khalapvau shreshthau, khalapvam cha khalapvi cha" (declension).
Thus sharapu and the like; kroshtu: "kroshta, krostarah, kroshtun cha, kroshtuna, kroshtra, kroshtunam, kroshtari" (declension).
Pitri: "pita, pitarau, pitarah, he pitah, pitarau shubhau, pitrin, pituh, pituh, pitroh, pitrinam, pitari" (declension).
Thus bhratri, jamatri and the like; nri: "nrinam, nrinam"; kartri: "karta, kartarau, kartrin, kartrinam, kartari" (declension).
Like pitri thus udgatri, svasri, naptri and the like; sura: "surah, surayau, surayah, surayam cha, surayyapi" (declension).
Go: "gauh, gavau, ganga, gava cha, gor, gavoh cha, gavam, gavi"; thus dyau, lau; vowel-ending masculine nouns (declension examples).
Suvach: "suvak, suvachau, suvacha, suvagbhyam cha, suvakshu"; thus dik and the rest; pranch: "pranch, pranchau, pranchan cha, bho vraja" (declension).
Pragbhyam, pragbhih, prachan cha, prachi cha, pranksu, pranksu; thus udanch, udichi; samyanch, pratyanch, samichi (declension).
Tiryanch, tirash, sadhryanch, vishvadryanch are remembered as before; adadryanch, adamuyanch, amumuyanch is told (declension).
Adadrynchah, amudrichah, adadryagbhyam cha as before; tattvatrit: "tattvatrit, tattvatrishau, tattvatrigbhyam samagatah" (declension).
Tattvatrishi, tattvatritsu thus kashthatad and the like; bhishak: "bhishak, bhishagbhyam, bhishaji" and janmabhak and the like (declension).
Marut: "marut, marudbhyam, maruti" thus shatrujit and the like; bhavan: "bhavan, bhavantau, bhavatam, bhavan, bhavati" (declension).
Mahan: "mahan, mahantau, mahatam" thus bhagavat and the like; thus maghavan, maghavantau; agnichit: "agnichit, agnichiti" (declension).
In agnichit-forms likewise another; vedavit, tattvavit; vedavidam thus another; sarvavit by compound (declension).
Rajan: "raja, rajanau, rajnah, rajni, rajani, rajan"; yajvan: "yajva, yajvanah"; thus; kari and dandi: "dandina" (declension).
Panthan: "panthah, panthanau, cha pathah, pathibhyam, pathi"; so too; manthan, ribhukshan, pathin and others, five, five and with five (declension).
Pratan, pratanau, pratanbhyam, he pratan cha, susharmanah; apah, apah, adbhih thus; "prashan cha prashamyapi" (declension).
Ka (who): "kah, kena, sarvavat, keshu; ayam, ime, iman, nayah; anena, abhyam, ebhih; asmai, ebhyah, svam, asya" (declension of pronouns).
Anayoh, eshamu, eshu; chatur: "chatvarah, chaturas, chaturnam, chatursu"; sugir: "sugih, shreshthah, sugirya" (declension).
Sudyu: "sudyauh, sudivau, sudyubhyam"; dik, vish: "vitsu"; yadrish: "yadrigbhyam, vidbhyam"; shash: "shat, shat, shannam, shatsu" (declension).
Suvachas: "suvachah, suvachasa, suvachobhyam" thus; "he suvachah, he ushanan, ushana, voshanasi" (declension).
Purandamsha; aneha; "he vidvan, vidvamsa uttamah, vidushe, namo vidvadbhyam, vidvatsu cha, babhuvivan" (declension).
And thus pechivan; shreyan: "shreyamsau, shreyasas"; asau: "amu, ami, shreshtha, amum, amunih, amuna" (declension).
Amibhir, amushmai, amushmat, amushya, amuyoh, amishaam, amushmin thus; godhuk: "godhuk, godhugbhir agatah" (declension).
Godhukshu thus others; mitradruh: "mitradruhah, mitraduha, mitradhrugbhyam, mitradhrugbhih"; thus chittadruh and the like (declension).
Svalit: "svalit, svalidbhyam, svalihi"; anadvan: "anadvan, anadutsu"; vowel-ending and consonant-ending masculines; now I tell the feminines.
Buddhi: "buddhih, buddhya, buddhaye cha, buddhyai, buddheh, hemate" — like kavi; of the sages; nadi: "nadi, nadyau, nadim, nadih" (declension of feminine nouns).
